content: {"rules": ["The model exhibits a persistent upward bias, consistently overestimating prices during periods of mean reversion or downward trends, particularly when the sentiment history is flat or zero.", "Forecasts fail to capture the magnitude of sharp price drops (overshoot on the downside), often predicting a slow decline while actual prices crash rapidly.", "The model displays significant lag in reacting to upward spikes; it continues to project gradual increases even after the true price has already surged, missing the initial breakout momentum.", "Sentiment signals (values > 0.00) are underweighted; the model does not sufficiently adjust forecasts upward when positive sentiment is present, nor does it react aggressively enough to negative sentiment implied by falling prices.", "Correction Rule: Apply a negative adjustment to the forecast when the 18-day history shows a downward trend or recent price drops, regardless of the model's smooth upward projection. Conversely, apply a positive momentum boost when the true price breaks above the forecast range to account for the model's lag in capturing rallies."]}
